title: vLLM — CPU/filesystem KV offloading tier *does* run on one GPU (negative hardware requirement)
hw: **None beyond one GPU.** Recorded here explicitly because it is the counter-cell: vLLM's `OffloadingConnector`/`TieringOffloadingSpec` offloads KV to CPU pinned memory and secondary tiers with `cudaMemcpyAsync`, with no RDMA, NVLink, or second GPU in the documented path.
evidence: This guide covers configuration of the [`OffloadingConnector`](disagg_prefill.md), which extends the prefix cache by offloading completed KV blocks to slower but larger tiers (CPU host memory, plus optional secondary tiers) as they are produced. Hits in the offload tiers are promoted back to GPU on demand. Transfers between GPU and CPU use DMA (`cudaMemcpyAsync`) and run asynchronously alongside model computation, so offloading adds minimal CPU- and GPU-core overhead.

title: Provable prefix-KV placement across a worker fleet (PrefixPlace)
hw: a multi-worker serving topology with cross-worker replica fetches (evaluated at 4/8/16 workers; measured across T4, L4 and A100 requester hardware)
evidence: Prefix Key–Value (KV) reuse avoids repeated prefill in Large Language Model (LLM) inference, but local misses require recomputation or replica fetches. Their relative cost varies with hardware, prefix depth, KV goodput, and replica location, making hit-rate-based placement suboptimal. ... "PrefixPlace solves a 50,000-node, 16-worker placement in 12.3 s on one processor, enabling timely replanning." The measured regime split is likewise hardware-dependent: "Recomputation is already slower on T4, crosses the transfer cost near 3.8K existing tokens on L4, and remains faster throughout the measured A100 range."

title: Cross-instance prefix sharing through a shared L3 tier (SGLang HiCache distributed backends)
hw: more than one inference instance / a cluster-wide storage namespace; L2 is explicitly instance-private, so any cross-instance reuse needs a distributed L3 backend
evidence: **L2 is node-local and instance-private.** It is host memory owned by one inference instance's process, so two instances never read each other's L2, not even two instances on the same node. A KV cache produced by instance 0 becomes visible to instance 1 only after it reaches L3. And: "Distributed backends such as `mooncake`, `hf3fs`, `nixl` and `aibrix` give cluster-wide scope, but only when every instance is pointed at the same namespace and configuration." Also relevant to the single-GPU case: "The `file` backend writes to `/tmp/hicache` by default (`SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR` overrides it), which is node-local unless that path is a shared mount."

title: HiCache host-memory sizing guard (`host_memory_budget_bytes`)
hw: multiple co-located ranks on one host (demonstrated at `--tp 8`); the guard divides free RAM by `ranks_per_host()`, so the double-charging bug cannot occur with a single rank
evidence: Splitting the free memory by the number of co-located ranks is only right for a reading taken before any of those ranks allocates. But each rank reads available at the moment it reaches the guard, and TP ranks reach it at different times: pinning a large host pool takes seconds and nothing synchronizes the ranks between pools.
